'''Robert Sh. Liptser''' ({{langx|ru|Роберт Шевилевич Липцер}}; {{langx|he|רוברט ליפצר}}; 20 March 1936&nbsp;– 2 January 2019) was a Russian-Israeli [[mathematician]] who made contributions to the theory and applications of [[stochastic processes]], in particular to [[Martingale (probability theory)|martingales]], [[stochastic control]] and [[Filtering problem (stochastic processes)|nonlinear filtering]].

==Biography==

Liptser was born in [[Kropyvnytskyi|Kirovograd]], [[Ukraine]] and spent his youth in [[Odesa]], Ukraine. In 1959 he graduated with the M.Sc. degree in electrical engineering from [[Moscow Aviation Institute]] and in 1965 he graduated with the second M.Sc. in mathematics from [[MSU Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics|Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics]] of [[Moscow State University]]. In 1968 he obtained his Ph.D. degree from [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]] (MIPT).<ref>{{Google books|kRzQDgAAQBAJ|Statistics And Control Of Stochastic Processes: The Liptser Festschrift|page=XI|text=Robert Liptser|plainurl=}}
</ref>

He held a Professor position at MIPT and worked in the [[Institute of Control Sciences]] until 1990, when he joined the [[Institute for Information Transmission Problems]] as the head of the Stochastic Dynamic Systems Laboratory.

In 1993 emigrated to [[Israel]] and lived in [[Kfar Saba]]. In Israel he held a Professor position at the School of Electrical Engineering in [[Tel Aviv University]], until his retirement in 2005.

==Research==

Liptser made several important contributions to the theory of martingales and to their applications in engineering and statistics.<ref>Kabanov, Yu. M., Liptser, R. Sh. and Shiryaev, A. N. [https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1070/SM1979v035n05ABEH001615 "Absolute continuity and singularity of locally absolutely continuous probability distributions. I."], "Matematicheskii Sbornik 149.3 (1978): 364-415</ref><ref>Kabanov, Yu M., Liptser, R. Sh. and Shiryaev,  A. N. [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF00366270 "On the variation distance for probability measures defined on a filtered space."], "Probability theory and related fields 71.1 (1986): 19-35"</ref><ref>Liptser, R. Sh. [https://doi.org/10.1080/17442508008833146 "A strong law of large numbers for local martingales."], "Stochastics 3.1-4 (1980): 217-228."</ref> This includes his study of the [[conditionally Gaussian process]]es,<ref>Liptser, R. [http://www.mathnet.ru/php/archive.phtml?wshow=paper&jrnid=ppi&paperid=1032&option_lang=eng "Conditionally Gaussian Random Processes"], ''Probl. Peredachi Inf., 1974, Volume 10, Issue 2, Pages 75–94''</ref> which play an important role in the [[Separation principle in stochastic control#Nonlinear filtering solutions|separation principle in stochastic control]].<ref>Bensoussan, Alain. Stochastic control of partially observable systems. Cambridge University Press, 2004.</ref>

He coauthored a number of influential books.<ref>Liptser, Robert, and Shiryayev, Albert Nikolaevich. Theory of martingales. Vol. 49. Springer Science & Business Media, 2012.</ref> His monograph "Statistics of Random processes: General Theory and Applications",<ref>Liptser, Robert S., and Shiryaev, Albert N. Statistics of random processes: I. General theory, 2nd ed. Vol. 5. Springer Science & Business Media, 2013</ref><ref>Liptser, Robert S., and Shiryaev, Albert N. Statistics of random processes II: Applications. 2nd ed. Vol. 6. Springer Science & Business Media, 2013.</ref> written together with [[Albert Shiryaev]] in 1974, has become an internationally renowned reference textbook among scholars working in stochastic analysis and related fields.
